_comment: Tier-walk oracles (TASK-118). Hand-derived from fixtures/c_repo/expected_files.json by reading the edge table, NOT by running the walker — the closure fixed point is exactly the property the walker could get wrong, so the oracle has to be independent of it. Salvages the closure semantics of the retired TASK-080 spec: fixed point, both directions, source-extends, and a single-hop control that must NOT over-report.

multi_hop.why: The scope_ripple chain. brand_router calls reconcile_txn (settlement), so a routing assertion ripples into settlement and on into messaging — the 'adding a brand also changes settlement' relationship. Reaching the fixed point requires FOUR hops and both edge directions.
multi_hop.note_reverse: txn_lifecycle appears ONLY in brand_router's used_by. A depends_on-only walk would miss it and everything beyond it — silently.
multi_hop._header_note: The .h members appear because an edge identity like `config/brand_rules` names BOTH brand_rules.c and brand_rules.h — one compilation unit. Resolving an identity to a single file would be order-dependent, so the walk resolves to all of them. The oracle was corrected to follow that rule after the walker surfaced the ambiguity; the fixed-point and both-directions properties below are unchanged by it.

single_hop_control.why: The over-reporting control. retry.c depends on error_codes.c and nothing else touches either. A correct walk reaches exactly two files; a walk that leaked into the global graph would return the whole repo and look thorough.

source_extends_map.why: The map-omitted edge, and the reason it matters. dispatch.c resolves its handler through an opaque vtable and, on a failed lookup, enters the bounded-retry path — an indirect call the parser cannot resolve, so it lands in unresolved_patterns rather than as an edge. The `errors` component is DISCONNECTED in the map, so a dispatch assertion's ripple stops dead at its boundary. Tier 3a reads the source, finds the edge, and feeds it to tier 3b — which is the difference between reaching the retry path and never knowing it was affected.

recovered_edge.evidence: dispatch.c's failed-lookup path enters bounded retry through the vtable; the parser records this in unresolved_patterns rather than as a depends_on edge
